proof: Profiles A, B and C run over the same cases on a real corpus and are compared case by case: baseline value, treatment value, delta, then wins, losses, ties, mean and median delta and a bootstrap interval. The experiment found a real ranking defect on its first run (graph expansion displacing the answer) which is fixed by ranking direct hits above expansion-only ones while reserving a small tail for expansion.
finding: Against profile A the structural profile improves recall by 0.875 (7 wins, 0 losses, interval [0.625, 1.000]). Against profile B it does not: recall identical on all eight cases, precision within noise, 2.25 more retrieval steps on average (interval [0.75, 4.50]), and a smaller top-K context whose interval crosses zero. The hypothesis is not supported over hybrid retrieval on this corpus.
audit: PARTIAL before this task: M3.9 compared profile means; nothing tested the hypothesis case by case.
limitations: The corpus is this repository, eight cases, one revision; the measures are retrieval quality and cost, not task outcome, which needs PX-020 and a live provider.
